questions.text:
Directions: In the following question assuming the given statements to be true, find which of the conclusion among given conclusions is/are definitely true and then give your answers accordingly.

Statements:

P > Q; B ≥ R ≥ Q; C = A; N > B = C

Conclusions:

I. A = R

II. R < A

options.text: Only I follows
Only II follows
Either I or II follows
Both I and II follow
Neither I nor II follows

questions.explanation:
Given statements: P > Q; B ≥ R ≥ Q; C = A; N > B = C

Combined statement: A = C = B ≥ R ≥ Q < P; N > B 

A = R → False (as A = C = B ≥ R →  A ≥ R → A = R or A > R. So, it is false)

R < A → False (as A = C = B ≥ R →  A ≥ R → A = R or A > R So, it is false)

But here, A > R and A = R forms complementary pair.

Hence, Either I or II follows.

Conditions of Either-or case:

1. The elements should be the same in both statements.

2. Individually both the conclusions should be false.

3. One conclusion should be positive and one conclusion should be negative (Complementary pair).

The two complementary pairs in the either-or case are:

1) All + Some not

2) No + Some

questions.text:
Directions: In the following question assuming the given statements to be True, find which of the conclusion among given conclusions is/are definitely true and then give your answers accordingly.

Statements: L < O < M ; Q > N ≥ P > M 

Conclusions:

I. P > L

II. M > N

options.text: Only I is True
Only II is True
Both I and II are True
Either I or II is True
Neither I nor II is True

questions.explanation:
Given Statements : L < O < M ; Q> N ≥ P > M 

On Combining : Q > N ≥ P > M > O > L

Conclusions :

I. P > L → True ( As P > M > O > L → thus clear relation P and L can be determined )

II. M > N → False ( As N ≥ P > M → thus we conclude that M is less than N not greater )

Therefore Only I is true.

Statements: B = A ≥ F; C ≤ D ≤ F

I. C ≤  A

II. D ≤  A

options.text: Only I is true
Only II is true
Either I or II is true
Both I and II is true
Neither I nor II is true

questions.explanation:
Given statements: B = A ≥ F; C ≤ D ≤ F

On combining:  C ≤ D ≤ F ≤ A = B

Conclusions:

I. C ≤ A → True (as C ≤ F ≤ A)

II. D ≤ A → True ( as D ≤ F ≤ A)

Therefore, Both conclusions I and II follow

Both I and II is True

questions.explanation:
Given statements: A < B ≥ C > D ; C < F ; E ≤ D

On combining:A < B ≥ C > D ≥ E ; C < F

Conclusions:

 I. A < F → False ( As A < B ≥ C < F  →  thus clear relation between A and F cannot be determined)

II. E < F  →True (As F >  C > D  ≥  E  → E < F)

Therfore only conclusion II is True.

Directions: In the following question assuming the given statements to be True, find which of the conclusion among given conclusions is / are definitely true and then give your answers accordingly.

Statements: N ≤ V > E = A; A < B; B = N > O; P < O

Conclusions:

I. V = N

II. V > N

options.text: None is True
Both I and II are True
Only II is True
Only I is True
Either I or II is True

questions.explanation:
Given statements: N ≤ V > E = A; A < B; B = N > O; P < O

On combining: V ≥ N = B > A = E; B = N > O > P

Conclusions:

I. V = N → False (as V ≥ N)

II. V > N → False (as V ≥ N)

Therefore, conclusion I and II forms complementary pair.

Hence, either I or II follows.

On combining: E > I > W ≥ L < B

Directions: In the following question assuming the given statements to be True, find which of the conclusion among given conclusions is/ are definitely true and then give your answers accordingly.

Statements: B ≤ F < T ≤ J; P > E < J ≥ M; A ≥ Q ≥ F

Conclusions:

I. E < A

II. A ≥ B

III. Q > M

options.text: Only III is true
Both II and III are true
Only II is true
Both I and II are true
Only III and neither I nor II is true

questions.explanation:
Given statements: B ≤ F < T ≤ J; P > E < J ≥ M; A ≥ Q ≥ F

On combining: E < J ≥ T > F ≤ Q ≤ A; P > E < J ≥ M; B ≤ F ≤ Q ≤ A

Conclusions:

I. E < A → False ( E < J ≥ T > F ≤ Q ≤ A) → thus clear relation between E and A cannot be determined.

II. A ≥ B → True (B ≤ F ≤ Q ≤ A) → A ≥ B.

III. Q > M → False (On combining: Q ≥ F < T ≤ J ≥ M) → thus clear relation between Q and M cannot be determined.

Therefore, Only II is true

Statements: V > R ≥ Q; C = B; X ≤ P < B; R > C;  

Conclusions:

I. R > X

II. X < C

III. B ≥ Q

options.text: Only II is true
Only III is true
Both I and II are true
Both II and III are true
Both I and III are true

questions.explanation:
Given statements: V > R ≥ Q; C = B; X ≤ P < B; R > C;  

On combining: V > R > C = B > P ≥ X; R ≥ Q

Conclusions:

I. R > X → True (R > C = B > P ≥ X → R > X)

II. X < C → True (C = B > P ≥ X → C > X)

III. B ≥ Q → False (R > C = B and R ≥ Q → Both B and Q are smaller than R and the relation between them can’t be determined.)

Hence, both conclusions I and II are true.
